focus: DESIGN SYSTEM — shared surface primitives, semantic roles, and landing order
noveltyJustification: The implementation already contains shared shell/header and record-surface seams, but the audit found repeated row/divider geometry, stale card tokens, and raw status palettes. A token-first and primitive-first landing order prevents children from fixing the same surface through competing selectors.

ruledOut.direction: treat the token list alone as a complete design system
ruledOut.reason: Repeated row, divider, header, status, and stack behavior still lives in consumer-specific CSS/builders.

ruledOut.direction: land independent child CSS in parallel on the shared stylesheet
ruledOut.reason: D4 keeps the CSS lane serial and overlapping primitive changes would invalidate dependent captures.

ruledOut.direction: add board-specific raw status/priority colours before role aliases
ruledOut.reason: Both-theme values and semantic foreground/tint relationships must be centralized first.
